findings: Linux full run 042 passed 28 core groups, then failed only the cross-process iframe image comparison in the screenshot group. The first image omitted the yellow child surface while all other outcomes matched.
Probe 043 found missing child pixels in the first two candidate captures on each of three iterations. Both engines included the pixels after rendering progressed.

Probe 044 varied raw CDP child interactions. Attachment alone missed pixels; evaluation/Page.enable/layout/two-animation-frame cases included them. These observations alone did not prove a synchronization guarantee.

Instrumented native trace 001 subsequently showed first-paint omissions in BOTH engines. Its added proxy overhead changes scheduling; it establishes a race, not latency or speed. All twelve candidate temporary child attachments had corresponding detach commands.
The screenshot fixture now waits for child and parent rendering frames before exact pixel comparison. Production capture adds no fixed sleep or animation-frame delay.

A separate blocked-child case demonstrates a real reference dependency: even unmodified screenshots evaluate child preparation and must time out when that renderer is blocked. Temporary child sessions preserve that dependency and cleanup. Both engines recover after child removal.

The first blocked-child fixture directly posted a message before a busy loop and hung in reference page.evaluate; its watchdog was intentionally interrupted. The revised fixture loads first, posts a deliberate blocking message, and gives the fault a turn before screenshot timing. Its timeout and recovery pass on native macOS.
